title: Record review
purpose: Close a submitted deviation or return it for revision.
summary: Close a submitted deviation or return it for revision. Managers and administrators only.

tasks.title: Close the report
steps: Choose Close in [[Decision]], explain in [[Reason]] and select [[Record review]].

tasks.title: Send it back
steps: Choose Return for revision and say what is needed.

good_to_know: You cannot review a report you created or last submitted.
A reason is needed for either decision.
A closed report can be reopened later with a reason.

sections.title: Access and meaning
paragraphs: Administrators, repository managers and technicians record, edit and submit deviations. Viewers read them. Managers and administrators review and reopen them. Inactive accounts and accounts without an application role, including bare superusers, have no access.

These are working product defaults, not repository policy. Deviations retain a report and its investigation, corrective action, effectiveness and independent review. They do not change specimens, stock, storage, linked records or holds. No attachments, deadlines, automatic notifications or risk thresholds are provided.

sections.title: Independent reviewer
paragraphs: The report must be Awaiting review. The reviewer must be a manager or administrator who is neither the original creator nor the latest submitter. No role or superuser status overrides this rule. A blocked form explains who must act.

items.label: Decision
items.description: Required. Close accepts this report and records the closure actor and server time. Return for revision restores Open status so operators can edit and submit again; the latest submission remains visible.

items.label: Reason
items.description: Required, up to 4,000 characters, for either decision. Explain the review outcome; it is retained in history.

items.label: Record review and Cancel
items.description: Record review saves the decision and returns to the report. Cancel returns without changing it. Review cannot edit the report narratives or related evidence.

sections.title: Saving and retained history
paragraphs: Every saved change requires a reason and records the actor, server time, revision and full prior and new values. Earlier narratives, source links, submissions and decisions remain in history. Reports cannot be deleted and history cannot be rewritten.

Saving validates and commits the report and its history together or saves nothing. Validation retains entered values. If someone changes the record first, your posted values stay visible and saving is blocked. Cancel, reload the latest record, compare your notes and start again; retrying the old form cannot overwrite the newer report. Do not enter identifying information.
